$comment: Extractor INPUT contract (WS-13 §3/§13; OmniRoute report §11.2). Hand-maintained and reviewed, in two halves. (1) `paths` is the VERSIONED path allowlist the sparse checkout materializes — the extractor refuses to materialize anything outside it and never widens the boundary on its own. (2) `providers` is the reviewed provider intake list: a row's `risk` is what the extractor stamps onto the generated WinterProviderDescriptor, and promoting one to "approved" is a deliberate, reviewed edit. No upstream source is vendored under this directory beyond the upstream LICENSE/NOTICE copies the extraction manifest records — see README.md.

importBoundary.$comment: WS-13 §3 step 2 says an import outside the allowlist "fails the job for review; the boundary never auto-widens". Taken as a rule about WIDENING, not about aborting: the literal extractor never follows an import at all, so a value that would have to come from an unmaterialized module is DROPPED with a recorded rejection (`unresolved-reference`), and the offending specifier is listed in the ledger's `outOfAllowlistImports` so drift stays visible. Aborting instead would make the pipeline unrunnable by construction — `open-sse/config/providers/shared.ts` imports a dozen modules outside any reviewable provider-data boundary. The boundary keeps its teeth through `failOnUnresolvedFields`: an allowlisted provider whose IDENTITY-critical field cannot be resolved from materialized files fails the run for review.

providers.$comment: `adapterIdOverride` because upstream's `format: "openai"` names its own DEFAULT execution path (Chat Completions), not the surface Winter drives. Six of upstream's own openai rows carry `targetFormat: "openai-responses"` — the *-pro and GPT-5.6 families are responses-ONLY, and upstream says so per model while its provider-level `format` does not — so deriving the adapter from `format` produced responses-only rows under a Chat Completions adapter. The overlay row has said `winter.openai-responses` since the seed, which is exactly what hid it: the merged catalog was consistent while the layer `--offline` validates STANDALONE was not. Found by extending that gate to the standalone layer (review r2 minor 5), which is the same shadow class as the Vertex adapter misroute.

The upstream id is `gemini`, not `google` — allowlistVersion 1 named `google` on both sides, which matched no upstream row at v3.8.50 and would have silently produced no google extraction at all. `winterId` stays `google` because WS-13 §12 and every seeded row use it.

providers.$comment: `adapterIdOverride` is Lane B's `VERTEX_ADAPTER_ID`, read from p6/lane-b's adapters/google/vertex.ts. Without it the mapper derives the adapter from the PROTOCOL, and Vertex shares GenerateContent with the Gemini API — so the extracted row named `winter.google-generate-content` and a registry, which resolves BY ID, would have served a Vertex session from the Gemini API adapter: no location-scoped URL, no ADC credential. The overlay row was corrected first; this fixes the layer `--offline` validates STANDALONE, which is exactly the layer whose defects an overlay shadow hides. `initialModelStatus: "experimental"` per R6-16 — the native-cloud families enter the catalog as `experimental`, and Lane B's `winter.vertex-gemini` adapter is live. Absent this field a row is `candidate`, which is what every other provider gets: upstream presence promotes nothing.

modelOverrides.$comment: ONE hand-reviewed per-model override map, applied by the mapper and RECORDED in the ledger as a `reviewed-normalization` — never a heuristic, and never silent. Three narrow things it can say about a single upstream model id: `id` corrects a wire id upstream spells differently from the provider's own documentation; `exclude` keeps a row out of the catalog entirely (WS-13 §4's MUST that non-`llm` rows never reach the worker-model picker — upstream has no per-model scope field, and a NAME heuristic would be worse than none because it would silently drop a future model whose id happens to match); `status` overrides the provider's `initialModelStatus` for one row. Every entry carries a `why` that ends up in the ledger, so a reviewer can diff the catalog against the pinned source and find every place they differ with the justification attached.

auto.why: OpenRouter documents its auto-router as the qualified id `openrouter/auto`; the pinned upstream entry lists a bare `{ id: "auto" }`. Keeping upstream's spelling put `auto` on the wire from BOTH resolution paths — step 1 (the seeded row's own upstreamId) and the `allowUnlisted` pass-through, which strips a self-prefix. Correcting it here fixes both at once, and the `auto` alias keeps the bare spelling resolvable.

gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview.why: A TEXT-TO-SPEECH model. WS-13 §4/§1 are a MUST: `tts` rows feed a separate subsystem and must never reach the Agent SDK worker-model picker, and the descriptor schema's `scope` is per PROVIDER — a `gemini` row cannot declare itself `tts` while its provider is `llm`. It also exposed the mapper's `outputModalities` default as a false claim: Winter stamps `["text"]` on every row because upstream declares no output modality at all, which for a TTS model is simply wrong. Excluded here rather than shipped as a resolvable `candidate`.

DeepSeek-V4-Pro.why: A Vertex MaaS PARTNER model. Upstream lists it under an entry whose `format` is `gemini`, so the mapper inherits the GenerateContent dialect for it — but partner models are not served over GenerateContent, and nothing has proven what they do speak here. `candidate` rather than R6-16's `experimental`, because `experimental` is a claim that a live adapter serves the row; flagged for Lane B/N.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash.why: As `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` — a Vertex MaaS partner model inheriting the Gemini dialect from a silent upstream entry.

categoryDispositions.$comment: WS-13 §1's disposition table, as DATA the extractor applies. `candidate-pool` means "eligible for the `providers` intake list above" — never "included": an api-key row absent from that list is still rejected, with class `not-allowlisted`. Every other category fails closed at import time, whatever the allowlist says (the check runs BOTH ways: an allowlisted id whose upstream category is not `candidate-pool` fails the run, which is the class transition WS-13 §3 step 7 blocks).

oauth.reason: WS-13 §1/§6: generic OAuth import is rejected; only provider-authorized product flows, which are Winter-owned rows, never extracted ones

apikey.reason: WS-13 §1: the main source pool, curated by LLM relevance and adapter quality — presence upstream is never inclusion

local.reason: WS-13 §12: the twelve chat/self-hosted backends are Winter-owned rows on live discovery (machine-specific inventories); image-only systems are excluded from worker models

audio.reason: WS-13 §1: not an Agent SDK worker-model provider

cloud-agent.reason: WS-13 §1: remote agent products, not model providers

blocked.reason: Image-generation system in the `local` category — WS-13 §1 keeps it out of selectable worker models (report §4.2).
Image-generation system in the `local` category — WS-13 §1 keeps it out of selectable worker models (report §4.2).

notes: `codex-oauth` is NOT extracted from upstream — it is a Winter-owned provider carried over per D11 with originator "winter" (WS-01 §3), and its descriptor's `upstream.project` is "winter".
The twelve local OpenAI-compatible ids (WS-13 §12) are likewise Winter-owned: their inventories are machine-specific and always come from live discovery, so there is no upstream row to extract.

Promoting a provider from `blocked`/`review-required` to `approved`, or adding an id to `providers`, is the reviewed allowlist change WS-13 §13 requires before anything can reach `supported`. The extractor has no other door.

`blocked` names INDIVIDUAL upstream ids only. It previously carried a `"*"` sentinel restating WS-13 §5/§6's categorical exclusions (browser sessions, private APIs, consumer subscriptions); the mapper filtered that row out, so it was documentation wearing the shape of a rule. Those exclusions are ENFORCED by `categoryDispositions` above, which fails the run both ways — an allowlisted id whose category is not the api-key candidate pool aborts extraction — so the sentinel is dropped rather than left looking load-bearing.
